Our mission
E-ACT at a glance
Opening Minds, Opening Doors
We will open minds and open doors for our pupils, our staff and our communities by:
Having uncompromising aspirations for all
Living our values
Understanding, celebrating and working with our communities
What we value
Our values are our anchor point and underpin all we do as a trust.
We want all of our 25,000 pupils and 3,500 colleagues to realise their full potential by our three values.
THINK BIG
for themselves and for the world around them.
SHOW TEAM SPIRIT
always supporting and driving forward together.
DOING THE RIGHT THING
in everything they do, even when this means doing something that's hard, not popular or takes a lot of time.
Did you know?
What it means to be part of a multi-academy trust
Our academies can collaborate and share ideas with one another in ways that schools may not be able to.
Should a teacher of history at E-ACT Crest Academy in London wish to seek advice on part of the GCSE history curriculum, they have the option to call on every other teacher of history within the trust for assistance.
Our academies can also rely on support, when it is needed, from our regional experts on both educational and non-educational matters. Our education directors, for example, will work very closely with the headteachers on everything from curricula development to classroom strategy.
For the teacher that joins an academy trust there are significant benefits too. Should a mathematics teachers aspire to become a head of department, they can maintain their employability within the trust but find a head of mathematics job in another of our academies.
Most importantly by being part E-ACT we all feel part of something much bigger. Our responsibilities go far beyond the four walls of a single academy, and extend to people and their communities across the country.

Personal Development
Personal Development Statement of Intent
Our intent is to nurture happy, healthy young people who have the knowledge, academic achievement and strength of character to lead safe and successful lives in modern Britain, preparing them for their next steps in education with a thirst for lifelong learning. We ensure that every member of our school community knows that we are committed to supporting their physical health, safety, and emotional wellbeing throughout their journey with us.
At Braintcroft E-Act Primary Academy our aims are highlighted in the school’s motto ‘Success in Everything We Do ‘and is also permeated through our core values of ‘SPIRIT’ (Success, Perseverance, Integrity, Resilience, Independence and Thoughtfulness) which embodies our attitude and intentions towards the importance of the development of all aspects of the Personal Development curriculum.
We promote Personal Development as a whole-school approach. All our pupils are encouraged to take part in a wide range of activities and experiences across and beyond the curriculum, contributing fully to the life of the school and the wider community. In doing so, pupils learn to recognise their own worth, develop a sense of their own identity and the ability to take their place in the community as well as respect for, and working with, others. There are many avenues throughout the school which drives our personal development curriculum forward. These include:
• Relationship education, Health education, Sex education
• SMSC (Spiritual, Moral, Social, Cultural)
• Our Trust and School Values
• Religious Education & Physical Education – Parents and carers have the right to withdraw their child from all or part of the Religious Education Curriculum. To do this please speak to the Class Teacher.
• Interactions with our pastoral team.
• Citizenship and Character Education
• Celebratory Days and Events
• Extended Learning Curriculum (Clubs and Classes)
• Promotion of Mental Health and Well-being
• Careers and Wider Opportunities
• Education Recovery
Implementation of Personal Development
Personal development is at the heart of our whole school ethos. We ensure each area of the personal development curriculum delivers all aspects of the statutory guidance and reflects our specific needs of our children and the wider school community.
We have staff and school leaders who delivers key areas of the personal development curriculum. SMSC and British Values, PSHE and RSE, Emotional Health and Wellbeing are taught alongside our Global Themed Curriculum by all staff. Senior Leaders and Pastoral Leaders ensures that assemblies also reinforce these key areas.
The Personal Development curriculum is delivered through every aspect of school life; every interaction with another child or an adult in school is a learning experience. It includes activities and experiences that improve awareness and identity, develop talents and potential, build character and cultural capital, enhance children’s quality of life and encourage aspiration.
Curriculum breadth shaped by our curriculum global themes: – Identity and Diversity, Social Justice and Equity, Peace and Conflict, Sustainability, Power and Governance, Human Rights which are linked to the United Nation’s seventeen Global Goals which allows our pupils to think critically about world issues amidst our commitment to delivering high quality education.
All aspects of the curriculum are mapped out in the overview of our whole school approach to personal development. Some are taught, some delivered through PSHE
Curriculum and RSE, other experiences may happen through visits and visitors.
Students are encouraged to develop their individual character, learn how to stay safe and healthy and develop knowledge to ensure they are well equipped for the future.

Governance Information
E-ACT is a multi-academy trust responsible for the governance and strategic oversight of all E-ACT academies.
The Board of Trustees is accountable for the performance of the Trust and its academies. Trustees set the strategic direction of E-ACT, oversee educational and financial performance, and ensure compliance with statutory and regulatory requirements.
Through its governance structure, E-ACT provides effective oversight while empowering academy leaders to deliver excellent outcomes for pupils.
Governance at E-ACT
OUR GOVERNANCE STRUCTURE
Members: Members act as the guardians of E-ACT’s charitable purpose. They ensure the Trust remains true to its mission and values and are responsible for appointing trustees and approving significant constitutional changes.
Board of Trustees: The Board of Trustees oversees the strategic direction and performance of the Trust. Trustees ensure E-ACT meets its legal obligations, uses public funds responsibly and delivers high-quality education across all academies. They hold the CEO and Executive Leadership Team to account for educational and financial performance.
Chief Executive Officer (CEO) and National Leadership Team: The CEO leads the Trust, supported by the National Leadership Team. Together, they implement the Trust’s strategy, oversee educational, financial and operational performance, and ensure academies receive the support they need to succeed.
Academy Headteachers: Headteachers lead their academies on a day-to-day basis, ensuring high standards of education, safeguarding, behaviour and pupil wellbeing. They work closely with the National Leadership Team to deliver strong outcomes for pupils.
Academy Ambassadors: Academy Ambassadors provide local insight, support and constructive challenge. They help strengthen engagement between the academy, its community and the Trust, but do not hold delegated governance responsibilities.
Scheme of Delegation
Our Scheme of Delegation sets out how decisions are made across our organisation and explains the different layers of governance that work together to support our pupils, staff, and communities. The Scheme of Delegation ensures clarity, accountability and effective governance across all E-ACT academies. VIEW OUR SCHEME OF DELEGATION
Further Information
Further information about E-ACT’s governance arrangements, including statutory governance documents, Trustee information, declarations of interest and annual reports, can be found on the E-ACT website.
If you have any questions about our governance arrangements, please contact the National Governance Team at Governance@E-ACT.org.uk.
Academy Ambassadors
Every E-ACT academy is supported by an Academy Ambassador Group. Ambassador Groups connect academies with their local communities, bringing valuable insight, experience and perspective to support the success of the academy and enrich Trust-wide governance.
E-ACT has established an Ambassador Group in every academy because local voice is essential. Ambassador Groups help ensure that each academy remains connected to its community and that the views of parents, pupils and local stakeholders help inform the Trust’s understanding of academy life.
Ambassador Groups are not governance bodies and do not hold delegated decision-making powers. Their role is to strengthen the partnership between the academy, its community and E-ACT through three key pillars:
Membership
Each Academy Ambassador Group includes the Headteacher and two Parent Ambassadors elected in accordance with E-ACT’s Articles of Association.
Groups may also include individuals from the local community who can contribute their skills, experience, networks and local knowledge to support the academy and its pupils. Membership is designed to reflect the diversity and needs of the academy community while bringing together a broad range of perspectives.
VIEW OUR CURRENT AMBASSADOR GROUP MEMBERSHIP
Ambassador Charter
All Academy Ambassadors are expected to uphold the values of E-ACT and work in accordance with the Ambassador Group Charter, which sets out the commitments and expectations of Ambassadors, academies, the Trust and the Board of Trustees.
Get Involved
We are always keen to hear from parents, carers and members of the local community who are interested in supporting the work of our Academy Ambassador Group.
If you would like to find out more about becoming an Academy Ambassador, please contact the academy directly.

Meet our Headteacher
Welcome to Braintcroft E-ACT Primary Academy
It is my great pleasure to extend a warm welcome to you on behalf of the entire team here at Braintcroft. As the Headteacher, I am thrilled to introduce you to our vibrant school community, where excellence in education is both our tradition and our aspiration.
At Braintcroft, we pride ourselves on providing a nurturing and stimulating environment that fosters both academic and personal growth. Our dedicated staff are committed to delivering high-quality education, tailored to meet the individual needs of each student. We believe in creating a supportive and inclusive atmosphere where every child feels valued, respected, and empowered to reach their full potential.
Our curriculum is designed to inspire a love of learning and to equip students with the skills and knowledge they need to thrive in an ever-changing world. From engaging classroom experiences to a wide range of extracurricular activities, we are dedicated to supporting each student’s journey towards becoming confident, responsible, and successful individuals.
We recognise that a strong partnership between home and school is essential for our students’ success. We encourage open communication and active involvement from parents and guardians, as we work together to create a positive and productive learning experience. Your support and collaboration are vital to the continued success of our school community.
As you explore our website, I hope you find all the information you need about our curriculum, facilities, and the many ways in which we strive to make Braintcroft a place where every student can shine. If you have any questions or would like to learn more about what we offer, please do not hesitate to get in touch.
Thank you for visiting. We look forward to the opportunity of working with you and welcoming you into our school community.

Ofsted report
It’s official, we are a ‘GOOD’ academy
We are incredibly proud that our academy has been rated GOOD in our latest Ofsted inspection. This highlights the outstanding work and dedication of our staff and pupils in making E-ACT Braintcroft Academy a fantastic place to learn and grow.
The inspectors were delighted with what they saw when they were at our academy for two days. They especially praised the commitment of our staff in ensuring all of our pupils are catered for depending on their individual needs.
Take a look at some of the comments from the report:
“Pupils enjoy learning because their teachers provide opportunities that are both meaningful and exciting. They want pupils to have ambitious goals for their future lives and to develop enquiring minds.”
Nurturing environment
“Pupils are both happy and safe. Leaders have gone to great lengths to ensure that all feel valued and cared for as members of the school ‘family’.”
“Leaders have high expectations of everyone. They encourage all pupils, including those with special educational needs and/or disabilities (SEND), to work towards the same learning goals in each subject. Pupils learn effectively and produce work of high quality. ”
“Pupils are polite and well behaved. They rarely need to be reminded to follow the high expectations for their conduct and attitudes.”

School Organisation
We are a three form entry school, which means there are three classes in each year group from (Reception to Year 6). All of the teachers and support staff work as a team, to ensure that the children receive a broad and balanced curriculum including all statutory requirements.
Teaching support assistants support across year groups, helping individual children and small groups with all aspects of their school life.
At the beginning of the academic year we hold a parent and child meeting for each class.
At this meeting the class teacher sets out exactly what you are to expect within the year your child is in their class. This is also an opportunity for you to ask questions and build a relationship with your child’s class teacher.
During the Autumn and Spring term we invite parents to have one to one meetings with their child’s teacher. During these meetings, the teacher will be able to explain how well your child has settled into the academy and what their behaviour is like.
At this point the class teacher will also share information regarding your child’s progress. You will be informed about your child’s attendance and the class teacher will also share ideas of how you can support your child at home and what your child needs to focus upon in order to progress through the remainder of the year.
These meetings are also an opportunity for you to ask any questions you may have and to look at the books in depth.
You will receive an end of term report that summarises the achievements that your child has made and the skills that they have acquired during the academic year up to that point. The report will also include what your child needs to concentrate upon in order to make further progress.
Please remember our staff are always accessible at the end of the school day.
If there is anything that you are unsure of then please make an appointment to see your child’s class teacher. We aim to work with parents as a team – that is what benefits the children most.

Why School Meals are Great – Primary
Healthy and Nutritious Lunches
We know that enjoying a nutritious hot meal at lunchtime is always better value than a packed lunch. It is easy to work out how much money you will save by not having to buy and make up packed lunches every day and for the time you save every morning too.
Another important factor is that the meals Aspens serve are nutritionally balanced and they provide a choice of healthy meals. The meat offered daily is always traditional and halal. Our meals are £2.30 per day and freshly cooked daily on site by our caterers Aspens. We have healthy options available each day and have themed meal days too such as Italian day.
